street.note: French u in rue is close to Finnish y; ou in roue is close to Finnish u. Round your lips and keep the vowel steady.

two.note: Eu in deux is near Finnish ö, with tighter rounding. Ou in doux is near Finnish u. The final x is silent in these words here.

train.note: Train ends in a nasal vowel: air also passes through the nose, without a separate Finnish n. Trait ends in an oral vowel; its t is silent.

bread.note: Pain has a nasal vowel, without a separate final n. Paix has an oral vowel and a silent x. Listen for the vowel, not a consonant ending.

fish.note: Double ss in poisson makes an s sound. Single s between the vowels in poison makes a voiced z. Keep your voice buzzing for z.

dessert.note: Dessert has an s sound; désert has a voiced z. Double ss is a useful spelling anchor. In both words, the final t is silent.

hot.note: Chaud starts with sh /ʃ/; seau starts with s. Au and eau both make an o-like vowel here. The final d in chaud is silent.

three.note: Listen for the first consonant: trois starts with t; droit starts with voiced d. Oi is /wa/ in both. The written final consonant is silent here.

price.note: Prix starts with p; bris starts with voiced b. Keep the b voiced before r. Neither word ends with a pronounced s or x here.

without.note: These are two different nasal vowels. Sans has the an sound; son has the on sound. Neither ends with a separate Finnish n here.

rain.note: In pluie, start with the lip rounding of Finnish y and glide quickly into i, keeping one syllable. Pli has only the i vowel.
